final_report.root_cause: A Kubernetes Service misconfiguration: the post-storage-service Service maps port 9090 to targetPort 9999, but the post-storage container listens on 9090. Endpoints were created for the pod at port 9999 (10.244.1.36:9999), so kube-proxy routed ClusterIP traffic to a closed port on the pod. This caused persistent connection refusals for Thrift RPCs from compose-post-service (and cascading failures up the call chain).

These data points correlate to show the Service routes to the wrong port (9999) while the process listens on 9090, producing connection refused errors.
final_report.investigation_summary: Priority-1 and -2 investigations were completed. Steps: inspected pod specs and logs for post-storage-service and compose-post-service, fetched ConfigMaps (service-config.json) showing client expectations (9090), described the post-storage-service Kubernetes Service and Endpoints, and correlated endpoints with pod IP and containerPort. The investigations established that pods are running and healthy (no restarts/ooms), the post-storage process started, and the only failing element is traffic routing via the Service to the incorrect targetPort (9999). The causal chain: compose-post-service attempted Thrift RPCs to post-storage-service:9090 -> kube-proxy forwarded to pod:9999 (Endpoint) -> port 9999 closed -> connection refused -> compose-request failures -> nginx observed compose failures and returned errors upstream. The misconfigured Service is therefore the root cause. No further data collection was required to localize the fault.
